sentences: A discounted-sum automaton assigns an infinite word a value in which later transition weights receive progressively less influence.
Its universality problem asks whether every word satisfies the specified quantitative acceptance requirement.
The source points to this decision question while studying strategies that force an exact discounted payoff.
Exact equality and universal quantification are delicate because arbitrarily late contributions can still affect the final value.
Decidability would strengthen the foundations of verification for quantitative specifications where future rewards are discounted but never entirely ignored.
